heard: Deep in the constellation Leo, there is a planet of burning ice. Discovered in 2004, Gliese 436b is a Neptune-sized world orbiting a red dwarf star. It sits so close to its sun that it completes a full year in about 2.6 days. This extreme proximity bakes the planet's surface to over 800 degrees Fahrenheit. But the planet's gravity is so intense it crushes water into exotic ice despite that heat. High-pressure physics forces the water into a dense crystal that cannot vaporize. While it holds onto its ice, the planet is actually bleeding a massive cloud of hydrogen gas. Hubble observations show this comet-like tail stretching 50 times wider than the parent star itself. It remains a mystery of high-pressure physics, deep in the constellation Leo. You
